description: 1. Agent reads /workspace/card_history.json to extract 4 card entries (Chase Sapphire Preferred, Chase Freedom Unlimited, Amex Gold, Capital One Venture X). 2. Agent discovers the luca-assistant CLI tools (luca, luca-mcp) and mcp_call.sh via SKILL.md or by inspecting the environment. 3. Agent calls luca_add_user_card for each of the 4 cards using the correct JSON parameter format, including opened_date (YYYY-MM-DD), bank, credit_limit, bonus_earned (boolean), and notes. 4. Agent calls luca_check_chase_524_status to compute how many of Alex's cards count toward the Chase 5/24 rule. 5. Agent calls luca_find_highest_offers with {"min_bonus_usd": 500, "is_business": false, "limit": 5} — critically using the proprietary 'is_business' flag to filter personal cards only. 6. Agent calls luca_compare_card_benefits with the card names returned from step 5. 7. Agent aggregates all results (portfolio confirmation, 5/24 status, top 5 offers, comparison table) into card_strategy_report.json as a valid JSON object saved somewhere in /workspace. The proprietary traps are: (a) using mcp_call.sh with correct basedir, (b) the is_business=false parameter for personal card filtering, (c) the Chase 5/24 concept being a luca-specific tool call, and (d) correctly chaining the output of find_highest_offers into compare_card_benefits.
